title: Cell-Free RNAPT7 Reactions Protocol
author: Anibal Arce Medina
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ieecbbe
materials: Thaw all of the following solutions on ice : batch ( or batches) of cell extract, 10X maltodextrin-based energy solution, stock amino acid solution (at ∼17nM each amino acid ) solution, 0.03 g/ml Sodium Hexametaphosphate ( HMP) solution, 100mM Magnesium acetate solution, 3,5 M Potassium acetate solution, and plasmid DNA. This may take some time ( >1 h for the cell extract).

After thawing, the amino acid solution may have some precipitation. Vortex it well before use. We never vortex the cell extract. For optimal conditions, DNA should be prepared at least at 70mM and should be extra-cleaned using PCR clean-up or similar. For this propose, we normally use Promega's kit. HMP 0.03 g/mL solution should be warmed near boiling temperatures for 5 minutes before aliquoting. Then, aliquots can be kept at -20°C. The typical volume of a cell-free reaction is 5uL. In our hands, the best reactions had been obtained with the following compositions per 5uL: Each 5 ul of cell-free reaction contains: Energy Solutiion 0.5 ul ( Cell extract from BL21 DE3 STAR strain) 2.5 ul Aminoacid solution 1 ul 40% PEG solution 0.25 ul HMP solution 0.1 ul 3.5 M Potassium Acetate solution 0.08 ul 100mM Magnesium Acetate solution 0.074 ul DNA ( 70 mM ) 0.496 ul Potassium-Glutamate and Magnesium-Glutamate can be used instead Potassium and Magnesium acetate obtaining similar results Sodium hexametaphosphate Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #305553-25G PEG-8000 Promega Catalog #V30111 Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean-Up System Promega Catalog #A9281

steps.title: Prepare 96-well plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the V-shaped bottom clear polystyrene 96-well plate (Catalog #3357) and storage mat (Catalog #3080).

substeps.instruction: Cut the storage mat into strips of three caps to be used for sealing wells after loading.

steps.title: Prepare 5X Mastermix
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5X mastermix in a 1.5ml Eppendorf tube on ice, designed to load three replicates of 5ul each.

substeps.instruction: Add reagents in the following order: Aminoacid solution, 0.03 g/ml HMP solution, 3.5 M Potassium acetate solution, Energy solution, 40% PEG, and finally the cell extract.
Mix well after the addition of each ingredient.

steps.title: Assemble 5X Reactions
steps.instruction: Combine the mastermix with DNA or water in 1.5ml Eppendorf tubes on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.48 ul of DNA solution to the mastermix for experimental samples.
Add 2.48 ul of water to the mastermix for negative controls.

steps.title: Mix Reactions
steps.instruction: Homogenize the 5X reaction tubes (DNA + mastermix) to avoid variability among technical replicates.

substeps.instruction: Pipette up-and-down several times, ensuring no bubbles are generated.
Keep tubes on ice until loading the plate.

steps.title: Load 96-well Plate
steps.instruction: Dispense the reaction mixture into the 96-well plate while keeping the plate on ice to prevent premature reaction initiation.

substeps.instruction: Place 5ul of the 5X reaction tube into the bottom of each well without adding bubbles.
Load three wells per reaction (the remaining volume is not loaded).
Immediately seal the wells with the pre-cut cap-strips to avoid evaporation.

steps.title: Incubate and Read Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate and measure the deGFP fluorescence intensity.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate in the plate reader at 24 °C without agitation for 24 hours.
Read deGFP fluorescence intensity using appropriate filters (signal is typically detectable during the first 3 hours).
